info.name: M9_10
info.description:
## CodeBloggs API — M9_10

---

## Setup Instructions

### 1. Import this collection
Open Postman → **Import** → drag this file in. The collection and its variables load automatically.

### 2. Verify the base URL
The collection ships with `base_url = http://localhost:5050`. If your server runs on a different port, click the collection name → **Variables** tab and update the `base_url` current value.

### 3. Start the server
```bash
cd server && npm start
```
Wait for `🚀 Server listening on port 5050` before sending any requests.

### 4. Enable cookies (critical for auth)
- **Postman Desktop** — cookies are captured and replayed automatically. Nothing extra needed.
- **Postman Web** — install the **Postman Interceptor** browser extension. Without it, the `session_token` cookie set by `POST /session` will not be forwarded on subsequent requests and `GET /session/validate` will return 401.

### 5. Run in the recommended order
Requests are organized into seven folders. Run them **top to bottom** starting with **User**, then **Session**, then **Presence**, then **Posts**, then **Comments**, then **Replies**, then **Profile Pic**.

---

## Auto-captured collection variables

Four requests save MongoDB `_id` values into collection variables automatically via test scripts — no manual copy-paste required.

| Variable | Populated by | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `user_id` | POST /user | GET /user/:id · GET /profile-pic/:userId |
| `post_id` | POST /posts | PATCH /posts/:id · POST /comments · GET /replies · POST /replies |
| `comment_id` | POST /comments | PATCH /comments/:id · POST /replies (as parent_id) |
| `reply_id` | POST /replies | PUT /replies/:id |

---

## Presence

`GET /presence` returns the list of MongoDB user `_id` values that are currently online. It requires an active session cookie — the same request also acts as a heartbeat, refreshing the caller's own presence window.

---

## Recommended run order

```
1.  POST   /user                        → Register (captures user_id)
2.  POST   /session                     → Login (sets session cookie)
3.  GET    /session/validate            → Confirm session is live
4.  GET    /presence                    → List active user IDs (also heartbeats the caller)
5.  GET    /user                        → List all users
6.  GET    /user/{{user_id}}            → Fetch your registered user
7.  POST   /posts                       → Create a post (captures post_id)
8.  GET    /posts                       → List all posts
9.  PATCH  /posts/{{post_id}}           → Increment likes
10. POST   /comments                    → Add a comment (captures comment_id)
11. GET    /comments                    → List all comments
12. PATCH  /comments/{{comment_id}}     → Edit the comment
13. POST   /replies                     → Add a reply to the comment (captures reply_id)
14. GET    /replies?post_id={{post_id}} → List all replies for the post
15. PUT    /replies/{{reply_id}}        → Increment reply likes
16. POST   /profile-pic                 → Upload a profile picture
17. GET    /profile-pic/{{user_id}}     → Fetch the profile picture
18. DELETE /session                     → Logout (run last)
```

---

## Notes
- All JSON responses follow the shape `{ status, data, message }`.
- `time_stamp` is generated server-side on create for posts, comments, and replies — do not send it in request bodies.
- `user_id` on posts, comments, and replies is taken from the session cookie by the `requireSession` middleware — do not send it in request bodies.
- `likes`, `comments[]`, `auth_level`, and `status` are always set server-side and are ignored if sent in create request bodies.
- `GET /profile-pic/:userId` returns raw image binary (not JSON) — open it in a browser or Postman's image preview to see the picture.

variable.description: Base URL for the CodeBloggs backend API.

item.name: User
item.description: User registration and retrieval endpoints. Run 'Create User' first — it populates {{user_id}} for downstream requests.

request.description:
Register a new user account.

**Required:** `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `password`, `birthday`
**Optional:** `location`, `occupation`

`auth_level` and `status` are always set server-side (`basic` / `true`). The password is hashed with bcrypt and never returned.

Returns **201** on success. The test script captures `data.user._id` into `{{user_id}}`.
Retrieve all registered users. Passwords are excluded from every returned document. Returns an empty array when no users exist.

Retrieve a single user by their MongoDB `_id`. Uses `{{user_id}}` captured by **Create User**.

Returns **404** if the ID is not found or is malformed.

exec: pm.test('Returns a single user without password', () => {

item.name: Session
item.description: Cookie-based authentication. Login sets an HTTP-only `session_token` cookie that Postman forwards automatically on all subsequent requests.

request.description:
Authenticate with email and password. On success the server sets an HTTP-only `session_token` cookie (TTL: 24 hours). Postman captures this cookie automatically — no manual token handling needed.

**Use the same credentials you used in Create User.**

Returns **401** for invalid credentials (same message for wrong email or wrong password — by design).

exec: pm.test('Login response is ok and returns user', () => {

request.description:
Confirm the current `session_token` cookie maps to a live, unexpired session. Returns the associated user on success.

Run this after Login to verify the cookie is being forwarded correctly. Returns **401** if unauthenticated or the session has expired (> 24 hours old).

exec: pm.test('Session is valid and returns user', () => {

request.description:
Destroy the current session. The server deletes the `Session` document from MongoDB and clears the `session_token` cookie.

**Run this last.** This endpoint is idempotent — it returns 200 even if no active session exists.

item.name: Presence
item.description: Real-time presence. Requires an active session cookie — the request also doubles as a heartbeat, refreshing the caller's presence window.

request.description:
Return an array of MongoDB user `_id` strings that are currently online. **Requires an active session cookie** — run Login first.

Because `requireSession` refreshes presence on every authenticated request, calling this endpoint also acts as a heartbeat: it extends the caller's own online window without a separate call.

Returns **200** with `data.activeUserIds` (string array) on success. Returns **401** if no valid session cookie is present.

item.name: Posts
item.description: Blog post CRUD. Requires an active session cookie (run Login first). Create Post populates {{post_id}} for update requests.

request.description:
Create a new blog post. **Requires an active session cookie** — run Login first.

**Required:** `content`

`user_id` is resolved from the session cookie by the `requireSession` middleware and never read from the request body. `time_stamp` is generated server-side as an ISO 8601 string. `likes` starts at `0` and `comments` starts as `[]` — all set server-side.

Returns **201** on success. Returns **401** if no valid session cookie is present. The test script captures `data.post._id` into `{{post_id}}`.
Retrieve all blog posts. Returns an empty array when none exist.

Partial update for a post. Only `likes` is accepted — `content`, `user_id`, `time_stamp`, and all other fields are ignored even if sent. Uses `{{post_id}}` captured by **Create Post**.

Like de-duplication is handled client-side via localStorage (see Issues.md #11) — the server stores only the raw `likes` count.

Returns **404** if the ID is not found or is malformed.

item.name: Comments
item.description: Comment CRUD. Requires an active session cookie and {{post_id}} from the Posts folder. Create Comment populates {{comment_id}}.

request.description:
Add a comment to an existing post. **Requires an active session cookie** — run Login first.

**Required:** `content`, `post_id` (must reference an existing post)

`user_id` is resolved from the session cookie by the `requireSession` middleware and never read from the request body. `time_stamp` is generated server-side. The server verifies the parent post exists before saving, and pushes the new comment's `_id` onto the parent `Post.comments[]` array (two-way link). `likes` is always initialized to `0`.

Returns **401** if no valid session cookie is present. Returns **404** if `post_id` does not match any post. Returns **201** on success. The test script captures `data.comment._id` into `{{comment_id}}`.
Retrieve all comments across all posts. Returns an empty array when none exist.

Edit an existing comment. Both `content` and `likes` are accepted — send either or both. `post_id`, `user_id`, and `time_stamp` are permanently fixed at creation and are ignored even if sent. Uses `{{comment_id}}` captured by **Create Comment**.

Returns **404** if the ID is not found or is malformed.

item.name: Replies
item.description: Nested reply CRUD. Requires an active session cookie and {{post_id}} / {{comment_id}} from earlier folders. Supports up to 3 levels of nesting (depth 1–3). Create Reply populates {{reply_id}}.

request.description:
Add a reply to a comment or another reply. **Requires an active session cookie** — run Login first.

**Required:** `content`, `parent_id`, `parent_type`, `root_comment_id`, `post_id`, `depth`

- `parent_id` — MongoDB `_id` of the comment or reply being replied to.
- `parent_type` — `"Comment"` when replying directly to a comment; `"Reply"` when replying to an existing reply.
- `root_comment_id` — always the top-level comment's `_id`, even for deeply nested replies. Used to reconstruct the thread.
- `depth` — nesting level (1 = direct reply to a comment, 2 = reply to a depth-1 reply, 3 = max depth). The server clamps this to 1–3.

`user_id` is resolved from the session cookie. `time_stamp` is generated server-side. `likes` is initialized to `0`.

The server verifies the parent exists before saving. Returns **404** if the parent is not found. Returns **401** if no valid session cookie is present. Returns **201** on success. The test script captures `data.reply._id` into `{{reply_id}}`.

query.description: MongoDB _id of the post whose replies you want to retrieve.

request.description:
Retrieve all replies for a given post as a flat array ordered by `time_stamp` ascending. Uses `{{post_id}}` captured by **Create Post**.

**Required query param:** `post_id` — the server returns **400** if omitted.

The client reconstructs the nested tree by grouping replies by `parent_id`. Returns an empty array when no replies exist for the post.

Increment or decrement a reply's like count. Uses `{{reply_id}}` captured by **Create Reply**.

`likes` is applied as an increment via `$inc` — send `1` to add a like, `-1` to remove one. All other fields are ignored.

Returns **404** if the ID is not found or is malformed.

item.name: Profile Pic
item.description: Profile picture upload and retrieval. Upload requires an active session cookie. The GET endpoint is public — no session needed.

formdata.description: JPEG or PNG image file. Maximum size: 2 MB.

request.description:
Upload or replace the current user's profile picture. **Requires an active session cookie** — run Login first.

Send the image as `multipart/form-data` with the field key `image`. Accepted types: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`. Maximum size: **2 MB**.

`user_id` is resolved from the session cookie — do not send it in the body. If the user already has a profile picture, it is replaced (upsert).

Returns **400** if no file is provided, the file exceeds 2 MB, or the MIME type is unsupported. Returns **401** if no valid session cookie is present. Returns **200** on success with an empty `data` object.

Retrieve a user's profile picture as raw image binary. Uses `{{user_id}}` captured by **Create User**. This is a **public endpoint** — no session cookie required, so `` tags work without credentials. The response `Content-Type` is set to the stored MIME type (`image/jpeg` or `image/png`) and a `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` header is included. Use Postman's image preview panel to view the result. Returns **404** JSON if the user has not uploaded a profile picture or if the `userId` is malformed.

item.name: Module 10 Backend
item.description: Module 10 backend endpoints completed so far. Uses collection variables {{base_url}}, {{user_id}}, and {{post_id}}. Run supporting Module 9 create/login requests first when a happy-path request needs real data.

request.description:
Module 10 backend endpoint: PATCH {{base_url}}/user/{{user_id}}

Purpose: update allowed fields on an existing user.

Required headers:
Content-Type: application/json

Allowed body fields:
first_name, last_name, birthday, email, password, status, location, occupation, auth_level

Password behavior:
- Non-empty password values are hashed before saving.
- Missing or empty password values do not overwrite the current password.
- Password is never returned in the response.

Example success response, 200:
{
  "status": "ok",
  "data": { "user": { "_id": "{{user_id}}", "first_name": "Module", "last_name": "Ten" } },
  "message": "User updated successfully"
}

Example error responses:
400 malformed id: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "Invalid user id" }
404 missing user: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "User not found" }
409 duplicate email: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "Email already in use" }

Setup: run an existing supporting request such as User / Create User first, or set collection variable user_id to a throwaway user id.
Module 10 error scenario for PATCH /user/:id. Expected 400 with message Invalid user id.
Module 10 error scenario for PATCH /user/:id. Expected 404 with message User not found.

Module 10 backend endpoint: DELETE {{base_url}}/user/{{user_id}}

Purpose: delete a user and cascade cleanup related backend records.

Required headers: none.
Required body: none.

Cascade cleanup:
- posts written by the deleted user
- comments written by the deleted user
- comments on deleted user's posts
- related replies
- sessions for the deleted user
- profile picture records for the deleted user
- deleted comment ids pulled from remaining Post.comments[] arrays

Example success response, 200:
{ "status": "ok", "data": {}, "message": "User deleted successfully" }

Example error responses:
400 malformed id: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "Invalid user id" }
404 missing user: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "User not found" }

Safe testing: use only throwaway users. This request permanently deletes the selected user and related records.
Module 10 error scenario for DELETE /user/:id. Expected 400 with message Invalid user id.
Module 10 error scenario for DELETE /user/:id. Expected 404 with message User not found.

Module 10 backend endpoint: DELETE {{base_url}}/posts/{{post_id}}

Purpose: delete a post and cascade cleanup related comments/replies.

Required headers: none.
Required body: none.

Cascade cleanup:
- comments where Comment.post_id equals the post id
- replies where Reply.post_id equals the post id
- replies where Reply.root_comment_id is one of the deleted comment ids
- replies where Reply.parent_id is one of the deleted comment ids

Example success response, 200:
{ "status": "ok", "data": {}, "message": "Post deleted successfully" }

Example error responses:
400 malformed id: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "Invalid post id" }
404 missing post: { "status": "error", "data": {}, "message": "Post not found" }

Setup: run an existing supporting request such as Posts / Create Post first, or set collection variable post_id to a throwaway post id.
Module 10 error scenario for DELETE /posts/:id. Expected 400 with message Invalid post id.
Module 10 error scenario for DELETE /posts/:id. Expected 404 with message Post not found.
